Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by recent upper-respiratory viral illness (tight chest x 3 hours, wheeze, cough, mild exertional dyspnea).  
  • History of asthma since childhood; prior severe exacerbation requiring intubation and several-day hospital stay at age 16–17.  
  • Environmental allergies/hay fever (dust).  
  • Inhaler non-adherence last week (ran out of Ventolin and Clenil).  

- Relevant family medical history:
  • Mother: eczema.  
  • Father: asthma.  

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – ran out; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – ran out; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Oral corticosteroid course prescribed today (5 days, 2 tablets each morning) – specific drug/dose not documented.  
  • Spacer device prescribed.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

  • No self-harm ideation disclosed.

Management Plan

- Issued electronic prescriptions for:  
  • Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler for relief.  
  • Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler for maintenance.  
  • 5-day course of oral steroids (2 tablets each morning).  
  • Spacer device.

- Education provided:  
  • Use spacer for all inhaler doses; prime with two puffs, breathe 5–10 times.  
  • Continue maintenance inhaler once acute episode improves; use Ventolin PRN.  
  • Seek medical review if Ventolin required more often than every 3 hours, or if chest tightness, increasing dyspnea, light-headedness, or chest pain occur.  
  • Read steroid information sheet; advised re possible mood swings, hyperglycemia, rash, nausea, headache.

- Sick-leave: Advised rest; patient may self-certify first 7 days.

- Safety-net advice: Attend ED or call emergency services if symptoms deteriorate.

- Follow-up: No specific appointment booked; advised to arrange review if no improvement or earlier if concerned.

Consider (not actioned/not recorded):  
• Asthma action plan and inhaler-technique check at next review.  
• Preventive health updates (immunizations, smoking/alcohol assessment, BMI).  
• CTG registration and chronic disease management plan (EPC) if applicable.
